bubbleNote.blurb: LSU is the first team out at the 13 seed, sitting just one spot from the field. The Tigers are as close as a bubble team can get without being in.
Alabama sits at the 14 seed, two spots removed from the bracket. There's work to do, but nothing about that deficit is unrecoverable.
USC occupies the 15 seed, three spots outside the field. The Trojans need movement above them as much as they need wins of their own.
BYU holds down the last bubble slot at the 16 seed, four spots from the field. It's the longest climb of anyone still in the conversation.

games.blurb: The Apple Cup returns with No. 17 Washington laying 23.5 at home against Washington State, and a total of 50.5 suggests oddsmakers expect the Huskies to do most of the scoring. Rivalry games rarely respect a number this big, but Washington has every incentive to make an early statement.

A ranked-on-ranked opener: No. 24 Louisville heads to Oxford as a 6.5-point underdog against No. 9 Ole Miss with the total set at 55.5. The Cardinals can vault their whole season with one Week 1 road win.
Clemson opens on the road at No. 11 LSU, where the Tigers are favored by 10.5 with a 51.5 total. An unranked Clemson team can rewrite its September in Baton Rouge.

No. 19 SMU is a 2.5-point favorite in Tallahassee against an unranked Florida State, one of the tightest lines on the Week 1 board. The over/under of 53.5 hints at a game that could come down to the final possession.

No. 4 Notre Dame welcomes Wisconsin as a 20.5-point favorite with a modest 47.5 total. The Irish are expected to handle this comfortably, and anything less will invite questions about a top-five résumé.
The Border War kicks off the week with Colorado State favored by 3.5 at home over Wyoming and a total of 47.5. Neither side is ranked, but the trophy makes the spread mostly decorative.

predictions.blurb: BYU debuts at No. 15, and the advanced numbers are a shade cooler on the Cougars, with SP+ at 21 and FPI at 20. A Big 12 title path is there, but the models want to see it first.
Texas Tech checks in at No. 12 with the analytics firmly in its corner: eighth in SP+ and 10th in FPI. That's a profile that says the Red Raiders belong in the Big 12 driver's seat.
Washington opens at No. 17, right in line with an 18th-place SP+ rating, though FPI is more skeptical at 26. The Huskies' Big Ten schedule will settle the argument.
Houston lands at No. 23 despite metrics that aren't buying in yet, sitting 38th in SP+ and 35th in FPI. The Cougars will need results to close that gap.
Notre Dame sits at No. 4 with SP+ and FPI both slotting the Irish third, one of the tidiest consensus profiles in the country. As an independent, every week is a résumé week.

fieldStorylines.blurb: The Big Ten's automatic bid is the tightest race in the sport: No. 1 Ohio State leads with No. 2 Oregon a single spot behind. One slip from the Buckeyes and the Ducks are right there.
Georgia holds the SEC's auto-bid position at No. 3 with No. 5 Texas just two spots back. That's close enough that a single result could flip the league's playoff pecking order.
Texas Tech is the Big 12 front-runner at No. 12, with BYU three spots behind at No. 15. The gap is small enough that the Cougars stay very much alive for the league's automatic bid.
